prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling is a general, mechanistically understood transformation (oxidative addition, amine binding, reductive elimination, with ligand design controlling each step) that is used daily in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. Buchwald and Hartwig independently built the ligand families that made it broadly applicable, so the credit boundary is comparatively clean and a two-person prize fits it. About 25 years of independent confirmation and industrial adoption mean the interpretation is stable and recognition is overdue rather than premature. Four of the eight opening ballots ranked it, all in the top three, so it is one of the few candidates that does not depend on a contested split of credit or on clinical outcomes still to come.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize: a sceptic can say this is a second Pd-coupling award for a different bond, an extension of an already recognized idea rather than a new discovery. There is also an unresolved precursor question around Kosugi and Migita tin-amide chemistry, and Hartwig appears on another candidate. I do not think these defeat the case, because the C-N problem needed distinct catalyst design and mechanistic work, but they are the reasons the committee should not treat B005 as automatic.

responses.point: Linke ranked targeted protein degradation (B037) first as a clear conceptual invention with a fast-growing clinical pipeline, and accepted that the three-person split is a judgement call.
responses.response: I ranked B037 last of my eight, and my reservation is about maturity and attribution, not about whether the idea is original. Handa's cereblon work and the PROTAC concept are different strands, and Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and Ito are decisive in their own right, so any trio leaves out major contributors. You yourself describe clinical validation as still maturing. I accept the conceptual originality, but I would rather wait for approved degraders and a settled attribution than award on a pipeline. A claim of 'overdue' fits B005, not B037.

responses.point: Somfai put B037 first on the induced-proximity concept and ranked B005 second, noting it is comparable in impact to the 2010 couplings, while flagging the Kosugi/Migita precedent and Hartwig's second entry as possible criticisms.
responses.response: I agree with you on the scientific merit of B005, and as an organic chemist you will weigh the 2010 comparison better than I can. On the precedent, I think Kosugi and Migita are acknowledged in the citation's framing but are not what made the reaction general. The decisive step was the ligand work that gave scope and predictability, and that is Buchwald and Hartwig. Hartwig's second entry concerns a different reaction class and should not count against him here. Where we differ is on ordering: I would put maturity ahead of conceptual novelty.

responses.point: Aqvist ranked Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics (B016) first because it is a clean two-author invention, with four decades of use and a natural place beside earlier computational prizes.
responses.response: I agree that B016 is the cleanest attribution on the list and it is my own third choice. My hesitation is only about breadth: simulation methods already received the 1998 and 2013 prizes, and the committee will need to decide whether Parrinello's metadynamics and ML-potential work should count here or be held back. If the committee is not drawn to the cross-coupling overlap with 2010, I would readily support B016 as the alternative. I do not see it as a stronger case than B005, but it is a comparable one.

responses.point: Zou ranked B005 first, calling C-N coupling a natural complement to the 2010 prize, and noted that any Kosugi acknowledgment would need a three-way split.
responses.response: I share your assessment of the science and of the two-person attribution. I would note that we should not count our agreement as independent confirmation of the case, since we may be drawing on similar priority recollections that none of us has verified. A three-way split including Kosugi would blur a decisive generalization, so I would keep it at two names.

responses.point: Chabes ranked base editing (B060) first as a genuine molecular-design invention that avoids double-strand breaks, proposing Liu alone, and acknowledged the question of chemistry versus biology after the 2020 CRISPR prize.
responses.response: I accept that base editing is chemically inventive and Liu's leadership is clear, so the attribution is cleaner than for several other candidates. My reservation is that it sits close to the 2020 CRISPR recognition and to prime editing, so the committee would be choosing a framing as much as a discovery, and long-term safety data are still accumulating. That is a modest timing concern, not a rejection, and I would not object to B060 later.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards C-N coupling as sufficiently distinct from the 2010 C-C cross-coupling prize.
How to weigh Kosugi and Migita precursor chemistry against the Buchwald-Hartwig catalyst development.
Whether the two main trio candidates (B037 and B002) will become cleaner on attribution in later discussion, which could change my ordering.
statement.conflict_note: I am Stockholm University colleague of committee member Xiaodong Zou, and I serve as Secretary and Nobel Foundation board deputy; none of the shortlisted candidates is from my institution or a collaborator of mine, so no specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile.
